subject: Draft: Private deployment — license carveouts, audit playbook proposal
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: Private deployment — license carveouts, audit playbook proposal

Tom / Medix legal team,

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Per our follow-up, attached is a short proposal that splits the deployment exhibits into two pieces: (1) a lightweight Operator Rights Exhibit (what Redwood's operator may do inside the customer's VPC/on-prem host) and (2) a Customer License Exhibit (scope of customer use and data residency guarantees). The goal is to avoid broad source-code escrow while still providing Medix with verifiable auditability and a way to satisfy internal regulators.

Summary of what we propose: 
- Operator Rights Exhibit (attached: operator-exhibit-draft.docx): operator access limited to named operator accounts, read-only forensic snapshots via sealed snapshots, no remote interactive shell.
- Audit playbook: staged evidence delivery — quarterly sealed snapshots (hash + signature), 48-hour remote audit windows upon notice, and an on-prem witness option for once-per-year physical witness testing.
- Escrow-lite: sealed snapshot deposit with escrow agent (encrypted), plus an HSM key escrow handshake for emergency restore. This avoids escrow-ing source and keeps proofs auditable.
- Compliance package: SOC2 attestation + access logs export + runbook of operator procedures.

Attachments: privdeploy-runbook-summary.pdf, operator-exhibit-draft.docx.

Open questions for Medix: 
1) Would Medix accept encrypted sealed snapshots + third-party timestamping (instead of full code deposit)?
2) Do you require live operator witness access, or would a time-boxed witness recovery window + recorded forensic replay suffice?
3) Are there minimum retention/rotation windows for snapshots you need us to commit to in the Order Form?

Next steps: if you confirm the above approach is directionally acceptable, our legal and engineering teams will produce an Exhibit H draft and a short Order Form amendment to capture retention, audit cadence, and SLA carveouts. Happy to run a 30-minute call with procurement / security tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
David
David Kim
Head of Platform Security & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: privdeploy-runbook-summary.pdf (6 pages), operator-exhibit-draft.docx (draft)

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@medixhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, legal@medixhealth.com
Date: 2026-03-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Private deployment — license carveouts, audit playbook proposal

David — thanks for the thorough note. High level: Medix is open to a non-source escrow approach, but we need concrete proof points for our internal auditors. A few clarifications: 

• Snapshot cadence: quarterly snapshots are fine provided we can request an on-demand snapshot with 30 days notice during the first year (procurement requires this).
• Witnessing: we prefer a two-tier approach — remote forensic replay for all audits and an on-site witnessing option once per contract year (we will cover travel).
• Crypto: HSM-backed key escrow sounds acceptable. We need the escrow agent to be a recognized third party and to provide chain-of-custody logs.

I attached Medix's security questionnaire (partial) for your legal / security teams to fill. Also, procurement asks that any amendment include a clear PO and billing cadence in the Order Form.

Can you have a redline of the Operator Rights Exhibit and a short Order Form amendment by EOD Monday? We can then route to our legal for initial review.

—Tom
Tom Reed
VP Product, Medix Health
Attachments: medix-security-questionnaire.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@medixhealth.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Private deployment — license carveouts, audit playbook proposal

Tom / team,

Thanks — looping in legal redlines. I've attached a draft "Exhibit H — Operator Rights and Audit Playbook" redline (redline-exhibit-H-operator-rights.pdf). Key points we carved: 

1) Scoped Operator Role: operator identities must be named in Appendix A. Operator actions are limited to (a) rolling updates via non-interactive deployment API, (b) read-only forensic snapshot creation and retrieval, and (c) emergency restore using HSM-wrapped keys subject to dual-auth. No interactive shell access.

2) Audit Window: Customer may request a remote audit with 48-hours notice; Redwood will make relevant logs and snapshots available. For on-site witness events, Redwood will provide an agreed 5-business-day window and can optionally schedule a witness run.

3) Escrow-lite: We will use a recognized escrow agent (we propose IronSealed Partners or similar) for encrypted sealed snapshots. The escrow agent receives only the encrypted archive and a timestamped hash; key material remains with Redwood's KMS and an HSM-backed split-key escrow arrangement that is only decryptable under a three-party protocol (customer, escrow agent, Redwood). This provides a forensic path without handing over source.

4) Order Form language: retention (90 days for active logs, 12 months for snapshots) and evidence delivery SLA (48h for logs; 10 business days for a sealed snapshot delivery). Pricing: we propose a one-time deployment assurance fee (line on the Order Form) plus a monthly footprint charge; we will reflect numbers in the Order Form redline.

Open asks from our side: please confirm whether Medix needs the escrow agent to be named in the MSA or if naming the agent in the Order Form is sufficient for your auditors. Also confirm procurement PO timing — Tom mentioned PO in the next 30 days.

If Medix is okay, we can schedule a 30-min legal + security call Thursday at 10am PT to walk the redline and procurement expectations.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-exhibit-H-operator-rights.pdf (redline), suggested-orderform-amendment.docx (draft)

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@medixhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-16T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Private deployment — license carveouts, audit playbook proposal

Lauren / David — appreciate the clear redline. Medix is generally aligned with the escrow-lite approach and the retention windows. Procurement confirmed they can turn a PO in 30 days once we sign the amendment. A few quick points: 

• Please put the escrow agent name in the Order Form (procurement needs this line item).
• We accept the 48-hour log SLA and the on-site witness once per year.
• For pricing: please include the one-time deployment assurance fee and a projected monthly charge in your next redline (we need numbers to budget).

I'll have our counsel push back on any language that looks like source transfer; otherwise let's plan to take the redline you sent into our legal review. If you can send the consolidated redline + updated Order Form with numbers before EOD Monday, we will schedule the legal call for Wed and aim to have procurement PO ready within three weeks.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reed
VP Product, Medix Health

---
Thread notes: DocuSign for amendment expected after legal signoff. Procurement contact: legal@medixhealth.com.
